content.title: Partial update wipes fields: event-sourced store reduced the in-memory event (undefined keys) instead of the persisted JSON
content.problem: `eccode risk update --id RISK-1 --status mitigated` without --title/--severity/--owner removed those fields from the risk in the materialized project state (state.json, which `eccode status` and every later command read). The append-only log (events.jsonl) was correct. Because state() trusts the snapshot when its seq/hash match the last event, the corrupted snapshot became the effective state and later commits built on it. The only workaround was to re-send every field.
symptoms: After `eccode risk update --id <R> --status <s> --actor <a>`, state.json risks[<R>] has no title/severity/owner (mitigation also lost if omitted)
Re-running the update with all fields restores them
state.json differs from the state rebuilt by replaying events.jsonl (Store.rebuild()); replay keeps the fields
Regression test failure: 'state.json snapshot lost the title' while the 'replay of events.jsonl lost the title' assertion passes
content.component: ECCode lib/store.js Store.commit (event-sourced record); surfaced via lib/runs.js recordRisk + lib/reducer.js risk.recorded merge

steps: In a fresh temp project (tests/helpers.js tmpProject): eccode risk add --id RISK-1 --title 'Prompt injection' --severity high --mitigation validator --owner ai-engineer --actor product-architect
eccode risk update --id RISK-1 --status mitigated --actor product-architect
Compare .eccode/state.json risks.RISK-1 with new Store(dir).rebuild().risks.RISK-1: the snapshot lacks title/severity/mitigation/owner, the replay has them
Command: node --test tests/regression-risk-update.test.js (3 tests; all failed before the fix)

rootCause.explanation: Store.commit built the event object in memory, appended JSON.stringify(event) to events.jsonl, then called reduce(state, event) on the in-memory object, not on what was persisted. The CLI passes omitted flags as explicit keys with value undefined ({title: undefined, severity: undefined, owner: undefined, ...}). JSON.stringify omits undefined-valued object properties, so the log line is correct and replay merges correctly. But the risk.recorded reducer merges with object spread `{ ...existing, ...d }`, and spread copies own enumerable properties including those whose value is undefined, so the live reduction overwrote title/severity/owner with undefined; writeJson(state.json) then dropped those keys. Net effect: the snapshot (used as truth whenever its seq/hash match the log tail) diverged from the log. The code comment in recordRisk assumed 'undefined fields are dropped by JSON serialization, so updates keep previous values' - true for the log, false for the in-process reduce. Discriminating evidence: the regression test showed replay correct and snapshot wrong (ev:ev-muym6mgn-016c806e); a minimal experiment showed `{...{title:'T'}, ...{title:undefined}}` has own key title=undefined while a JSON round-trip merge keeps 'T' (ev:ev-muym6v1n-011b942a, exits 1 by design to show the mismatch). This is a general class (live state computed from a different representation than the one replayed), not specific to risks; risks were the only reducer that merges partial updates over existing records, so they were the first visible casualty.

failedAttempts.approach: Original design assumption (recordRisk comment): rely on JSON serialization to drop undefined fields so the reducer merge keeps earlier values
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Serialization only applied to the log; Store.commit reduced the unserialized object, so the snapshot saw undefined-valued keys and the spread merge overwrote existing values

failedAttempts.approach: Workaround used during the demo: re-run `risk update` with every field filled
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Masks the symptom per call; any later partial update re-corrupts the snapshot, and the snapshot/log divergence remains undetected for other event types

solution.description: Root fix in lib/store.js Store.commit: serialize the event once (`const line = JSON.stringify({...body, hash})`), append that line, then reduce `JSON.parse(line)` - i.e. reduce exactly what was persisted. Live reduction and replay now consume identical input, so the snapshot always equals a replay for every event type. Comment in lib/runs.js recordRisk corrected to describe the real mechanism. Regression test tests/regression-risk-update.test.js asserts field preservation via the CLI, deep equality of state.json / store.state() with Store.rebuild(), and the store-level invariant with undefined-valued data.
solution.tradeoffs: One extra JSON.parse per commit (negligible versus the fsync'd append and snapshot write). The `event` returned by commit() is now the JSON-normalized copy (no undefined keys, Dates as strings); all 45 existing toolkit tests pass, but an out-of-tree caller relying on object identity or non-JSON values in event.data would see a change. Alternatives rejected: stripping undefined in recordRisk or in the CLI (fixes risks only, leaves the class open for future merge reducers); making the reducer skip undefined (fixes only reducers that remember to do it). The fix does not heal snapshots already corrupted before it; deleting .eccode/state.json forces a rebuild from events.jsonl (the demo's RISK-1 had already been restored by a full re-update, and its snapshot now deep-equals replay). Verification ran only on Node 22.22.0/linux; the node >=18.17 range is the toolkit's engines floor and rests on ECMAScript semantics (object spread, JSON.stringify omission) rather than a run on older Node.

verification.regressionTest: node --test tests/regression-risk-update.test.js && npm test (in the ECCode toolkit root)

appliesWhen: An event-sourced or snapshot+log store computes live state by reducing an in-memory event object while replay reduces the serialized (JSON) form
Reducers merge partial updates with object spread or Object.assign and callers pass optional fields as explicit undefined (e.g. CLI flags mapped straight into a data object)
Symptom pattern: a partial update erases fields in the materialized state but replaying the log gives the right answer
Any ECCode record whose snapshot (.eccode/state.json) disagrees with Store.rebuild()
notApplicableWhen: The live path already reduces the persisted/parsed form, or state is only ever rebuilt from the log
Fields are lost in the log itself (events.jsonl lines lack the data): the cause is upstream of commit, not snapshot divergence
Intentional clears: a caller that sends null to clear a field (null survives JSON and still overwrites; that is expected)
Non-JSON persistence formats (structuredClone, v8.serialize, MessagePack) that preserve undefined - the divergence mechanism differs

solution.description: Root fix in lib/store.js Store.commit (commit 1f3c540): serialize the event once (`const line = JSON.stringify({...body, hash})`), append that line, then reduce `JSON.parse(line)` - i.e. reduce exactly what was persisted. Live reduction and replay now consume identical input, so the snapshot always equals a replay for every event type. Comment in lib/runs.js recordRisk corrected to describe the real mechanism. Regression test tests/regression-risk-update.test.js asserts field preservation via the CLI, deep equality of state.json / store.state() with Store.rebuild(), and the store-level invariant with undefined-valued data. Follow-up commit 2f3398c added an order-insensitive snapshot==replay check to `eccode audit` (detection) and `eccode rebuild` (rewrites state.json by replaying events.jsonl; repair).
solution.tradeoffs: One extra JSON.parse per commit (negligible versus the fsync'd append and snapshot write). The `event` returned by commit() is now the JSON-normalized copy (no undefined keys, Dates as strings); no in-tree caller reads it, but an out-of-tree caller relying on object identity or non-JSON values in event.data would see a change. At fix time the suite was 45 tests (42 pre-existing + 3 new regression tests), all passing; the reviewer later re-ran 46/46 including the 2f3398c audit test. Alternatives rejected: stripping undefined in recordRisk or in the CLI (fixes risks only, leaves the class open for future merge reducers); making the reducer skip undefined (fixes only reducers that remember to do it). The fix does not heal snapshots written before it: run `eccode audit` to detect snapshot/replay divergence and `eccode rebuild` to rewrite state.json from events.jsonl (do not hand-delete state.json). Verified environments: Node 22.22.0/linux (author) and Node 20.20.0/linux (technical-reviewer: pre-fix fail ev:ev-muymbyv4-01332d57, post-fix pass ev:ev-muymby0c-012fa681, full suite 46/46 ev:ev-muymc241-015f6d71). Untested hypothesis, not a verified claim: Node 18.x (the toolkit engines floor is 18.17) should behave identically because the mechanism rests only on ECMAScript semantics (object spread copies own undefined-valued properties; JSON.stringify omits them), but no run on Node <20 exists, so the environment is recorded as >=20.

reviews.notes: FIX AND ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED; LESSON NEEDS REVISION (env overclaim + over-broad appliesWhen). Checked: (1) Evidence chain: repro ev:ev-muym6mgn-016c806e really failed (exit 1, 3/3 not ok, 'state.json snapshot lost the title' while replay assertion passed) and verification ev:ev-muym78ex-01d9b8e9 is the identical command and passed 3/3; suite ev:ev-muym7byu-01f25152 45/45; experiment ev:ev-muym6v1n-011b942a shows spread keeps own undefined key, JSON round-trip keeps 'T'. All four logSha256 values recomputed and match the logs. (2) Reruns by me: regression test ev:ev-muymb01x-01ec5e0e pass 3/3; full suite ev:ev-muymb2za-016a248d pass 46/46 (now incl. 2f3398c audit test). (3) Independent repro: same test against HEAD~1 lib/store.js in a scratch copy fails 3/3 (ev:ev-muymb3qy-01495ec2). Scratch mechanism script outside repo: pre-fix reduce(in-memory)=undefined vs reduce(persisted)='T', snapshot!=replay, commit() returned corrupted state (ev:ev-muymb3xk-01517ccc, exit 1 by design); post-fix snapshot==replay, returned state correct, audit ok (ev:ev-muymb3uf-019c7deb). Fix is root-cause/general: commit now reduces JSON.parse of the exact persisted line, so live reduce and replay get identical input for every event type; hash computation unchanged (still sha256(prevHash+JSON.stringify(body)), undefined keys dropped identically), store.audit ok in scratch pre/post and 'eccode audit' OK on triage-desk (74 events). Read reducer: risk.recorded is the only merge-over-existing reducer whose result depends on undefined-vs-absent keys, so the 'only visible casualty' claim holds. Only commit() return value changed shape; no in-tree caller reads .event. Demo RISK-1 snapshot deep-equals replay (key order differs, content equal). REQUIRED REVISIONS: (a) environment {node: '>=18.17'} overclaims: the skill defines environment as versions the fix was VERIFIED on; it was run only on 22.22.0 (debugger) and now 20.20.0 by me (fail-before ev:ev-muymbyv4-01332d57, pass-after ev:ev-muymby0c-012fa681, suite 46/46 ev:ev-muymc241-015f6d71). 18.17-19.x is untested; the prose disclosure in tradeoffs is good but --check-env reads the field and would report 'applies' on 18.x. Set environment node '>=20' and notApplicableWhen 'env:node <20' (keep the ES-semantics argument for 18.x as an untested hypothesis in prose), citing the v20 ev ids. (b) appliesWhen bullet 'Any ECCode record whose snapshot disagrees with Store.rebuild()' is over-broad: divergence is a symptom with other possible causes (hand-edited state.json, non-pure reducer); after 1f3c540 this mechanism cannot produce new divergence. Narrow it to snapshots written by a pre-1f3c540 Store.commit where the missing fields are ones a partial update omitted, and name 'eccode rebuild'/'eccode audit' (2f3398c) as the repair/detection instead of deleting state.json. (c) minor: 'all 45 existing toolkit tests pass' - the 45 include the 3 new regression tests (42 pre-existing); reword. No change needed to code or tests.

VERIFY rev 2. Rejection reasons fixed: (a) environment now node '>=20' with notApplicableWhen 'env:node <20'; 18.x moved to prose as an explicit untested hypothesis. The Node 20 claim is backed: /opt/node20/bin/node is v20.20.0, pre-fix fails 0/3 (ev:ev-muymbyv4-01332d57), post-fix passes 3/3 (ev:ev-muymby0c-012fa681), suite 46/46 (ev:ev-muymc241-015f6d71). (b) the ECCode appliesWhen bullet is narrowed to pre-1f3c540 snapshots whose missing fields a partial update omitted, with eccode audit/rebuild (2f3398c) as detection/repair; a matching notApplicableWhen covers post-1f3c540 divergence. (c) test count is reworded to 42 pre-existing + 3 new = 45. I confirmed this with git grep test( counts (42 at 1f3c540^, 45 at 1f3c540), and ev:ev-muym7byu-01f25152 shows 45/45. Re-verified substance: my rerun of the same regression command passes 3/3 (ev:ev-muymf5s2-01d768f3). All 10 cited ev ids exist with the claimed status/purpose/exit: repro ev:ev-muym6mgn-016c806e, ev:ev-muymb3qy-01495ec2 and ev:ev-muymbyv4-01332d57 failed 0/3 as reproduction; ev:ev-muym6v1n-011b942a exits 1 by design; checks ev:ev-muym78ex-01d9b8e9, ev:ev-muym7byu-01f25152, ev:ev-muymb01x-01ec5e0e, ev:ev-muymb2za-016a248d, ev:ev-muymby0c-012fa681 and ev:ev-muymc241-015f6d71 passed. I recomputed sha256 of every log output and all match logSha256 in events.jsonl. The only spread-merge-over-existing reducer is risk.recorded (lib/reducer.js:222), and no in-tree caller reads commit().event. Security/integrity: the 1f3c540 diff leaves hash input unchanged (sha256(prevHash+JSON.stringify(body)) over the same body). JSON.parse only re-reads the line the process just wrote, so no untrusted input is added. My probe (ev:ev-muymg8r8-01d955e9) shows: audit ok after a partial update; lastHash equals the persisted hash; an edited event is flagged as a content hash mismatch; a __proto__ payload causes no prototype pollution and audit stays ok. eccode audit on triage-desk: OK, 85 events, chain intact. Pre-existing info finding, not caused by this fix: state() trusts state.json whenever seq/lastHash match, so a hand-edited snapshot is served until audit flags the divergence (probe confirms) and eccode rebuild repairs it. Privacy: rev 2 content has no emails, user paths, IPs or secrets; the scan's sk- hits are false positives from RISK-/risk-. Claims stay within the evidence.
